column1: qb5-h01|Repositioning remains necessary on a pressure-redistribution surface; individualize the regimen to tissue response and tolerance.|The client cannot shift weight without help.|New tissue change despite following the schedule.|A home setting does not make the mattress a replacement for repositioning.

qb5-h02|For a client unable to protect the airway, perform oral care with drainage positioning and controlled suction rather than free liquid or an expected rinse-and-spit.|The client cannot rinse, spit, or protect the airway reliably.|A safety precaution is being treated as complete protection.|Dry mouth calls for safe comfort care, not unsupported oral intake.

qb5-h03|During assessed acute panic, remain with the client, reduce stimulation, and give calm simple directions; defer complex teaching until attention improves.|The client cannot process a lengthy explanation right now.|Acute panic narrows the ability to take in information.|Too many voices are worsening overload.

qb5-h04|A capable adult controls consent during sexual-assault forensic care; pause or stop the requested step and discuss options without coercion.|The client is capable and distinguishes medical care from evidence collection.|Consent can change during the examination.|Acceptance of an examination is not blanket acceptance of every component.

qb5-h05|Use a rear-facing harnessed car seat in the back seat until the child reaches that seat’s rear-facing height or weight limit; fit follows manufacturer instructions.|A newborn needs a dedicated correctly installed restraint.|The child is still within the seat’s rear-facing limits.|Age alone does not mean the seat’s rear-facing limit has been reached.

qb5-h06|Routine neural-tube-defect prevention includes 400 mcg of folic acid daily before conception and during early pregnancy, not waiting for pregnancy recognition.|Planning pregnancy makes prevention relevant before a positive test.|Pregnancy can begin before the client knows it.|The label explicitly identifies folic acid rather than an ambiguous folate-equivalent number.

qb5-h07|Postoperative abdominal evisceration needs emergency surgical escalation and protection with a sterile saline-moistened covering, without bedside reinsertion.|Visible bowel after incision separation; help is already being called.|The protective covering is already in place; the unsafe extra intervention is the issue.|A transfer plan must change when evisceration appears.

qb5-h08|Maintain asepsis during central-line dressing care; correct contamination before contact with the prepared site or new dressing.|The glove touched a nonsterile surface before sterile-site care.|The surface that will touch the site has been contaminated.|The prepared site itself, not just a supply, has been touched nonsterilely.

qb5-h09|Assess pulse and toxicity cues before digoxin; withhold a dose and seek prompt review when hold parameters or concerning new symptoms are present.|A full-minute apical pulse is below this adult’s ordered threshold.|New gastrointestinal and visual symptoms matter even with a pulse of 72/min.|Diuretic-associated low potassium compounds new digoxin concerns.

qb5-h10|Distinguish potassium patterns using laboratory context: flattened T/prominent U waves support low potassium; tall peaked T waves can accompany high potassium. ECG does not replace laboratory assessment.|Low measured potassium with a prominent post-T deflection.|A high measured potassium value changes the interpretation from the earlier low-potassium case.|Compare two different laboratory-plus-ECG patterns rather than treating any abnormal wave as the same disorder.
